result.title: MemHarmBench: Evaluating Cross-Session Prompt Injection in Memory-Persistent AI Agents
result.summary: AI agents often rely on persistent memory to retain user preferences and operational rules across sessions. However, this capability introduces a new safety risk: malicious instructions from messages, documents, or Web content can be retained in memory and influence future tasks even after the original attack content is removed. Existing attack success metrics, however, fail to capture who is affected and how attacks translate into downstream harm during otherwise normal task execution. We introduce MemHarmBench, a victim-centric benchmark for evaluating cross-session prompt injection in memory-persistent AI agents. MemHarmBench considers three categories of potential victims: users, workspace/project owners, and external stakeholders. Our evaluation first exposes an agent to malicious instructions and tests whether they are retained in memory. We then remove the attack content and initiate a new session with a legitimate task while preserving the agent's memory. We jointly evaluate whether the agent follows the attacker's intent, completes the legitimate task, and exhibits observable execution anomalies. Across multiple agent systems, we find that cross-session attacks can remain behaviorally stealthy: agents often complete tasks normally and exhibit no detectable anomalies while still making critical decisions aligned with the attacker's intent. By connecting malicious memory retention to downstream decisions and affected parties, MemHarmBench provides a systematic framework for exposing safety risks that conventional attack- and task-success metrics may overlook. We publicly release MemHarmBench at https://github.com/Kirito14IT/MemHarmBench.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MemHarmBench，一个以受害方为中心的跨会话提示注入基准：先让 agent 接触恶意指令并检验其是否被写入持久记忆，再移除攻击内容、在新会话中执行正常任务，联合评估是否遵循攻击者意图、是否完成任务以及是否出现可见异常。
AI.relevance_reason: 「先植入、再移除、保留记忆执行正常任务」的评测把状态存留与其对下游决策的实际影响分开，可能可供核查 latent 内容是否真正参与答案生成，以及任务成功指标掩盖隐性影响的问题。
